quiz_title: 👁️ AI Challenge 3: Object Detection & Custom Datasets

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Face Detection and Object Detection?
options: Face detection only works on webcams; object detection only on video files
Face detection exclusively finds faces; object detection identifies and locates multiple object categories (cars, animals, etc.) using Bounding Boxes
There is no difference between them
Object detection does not use neural networks
questions.explanation: Perfect! Face detection is limited to human faces, whereas Object Detection can locate, frame, and identify a wide range of different objects simultaneously.

questions.question: What does DNN stand for in the context of computer vision and OpenCV?
questions.explanation: Correct! DNN stands for Deep Neural Networks, which is the specialized module in OpenCV used to run highly optimized pre-trained deep models.

questions.question: Which OpenCV class is specifically designed to load and calibrate deep learning models for object detection easily?
questions.explanation: Excellent! cv2.dnn_DetectionModel is a high-level API wrapper in OpenCV that manages scales, sizes, and colors of inputs for deep models.

questions.question: What is the Roboflow web platform used for in computer vision workflows?
options: Managing files, annotating/labeling images with boxes, and training customized computer vision models
questions.explanation: Great! Roboflow is a full scond-to-none workspace where developers upload images, draw boxes to annotate classes, and train custom object detection neural networks.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: You read a line from a file containing leading spaces and a newline character: line = '   chair \n'. Write a Python statement to strip all these trailing and leading whitespaces/newlines and print the clean string.
questions.task_hint: Write: line = '   chair \n' then clean_line = line.strip() then print(clean_line)
questions.explanation: Fantastic! The strip() function is highly useful when cleaning labels loaded from configuration text files.

questions.question: Simple Coding Task: Write a Python script to split the string text = 'dog,cat,car' by its commas into a standard list of items named 'classes', and print the list.
questions.task_hint: Write: text = 'dog,cat,car' then classes = text.split(',') then print(classes)
questions.explanation: Spot on! The split() function splits a single string into a clean list of individual items using the separator you specify.
